question.problem: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{4}{(x-1)^2}$ is defined for $x >1.$ Find $f^{-1}(x).$
question.worked_solution:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

$$
y = \dfrac{4}{(x-1)^2}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x = \dfrac{4}{(y-1)^2}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{4}{(y-1)^{2}} \\ x\cdot (y-1)^{2} & =4 \\ (y-1)^{2} & =\frac{4}{x} \\ \sqrt{(y-1)^{2}} & =\sqrt{\frac{4}{x}} \\ |y-1| & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}} \\ y-1 & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}} \\ y & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that for $y > 1,$ we have

$$
|y-1| = y-1.
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} + 1.
$$
